RequestSizeLimitingConfig.description:
Plugin: request_size_limiting — Per-proxy request body size limits.
Rejects oversized requests with HTTP 413 in three places: an early
Content-Length fast path (`on_request_received`), a buffered-body
check when another plugin already loaded the body (`before_proxy`),
and a final post-transform check before forwarding to the backend
(`on_final_request_body`).
`max_bytes` is additionally published to the proxy core as the effective
streaming/buffering ceiling, so unbuffered H1/H2, H3, and streaming-gRPC
uploads (chunked or unknown-length) are bounded at this route limit
before any byte is forwarded or retained. The effective bound is the
strictest active (nonzero) value of this limit and
FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES; a global limit of 0 means unlimited
and does not disable an active route limit, and multiple instances
compose to their minimum.
Repeated identical Content-Length values (RFC 9110 §8.6, which arrive
comma-folded in plugin-facing header maps) are parsed per member and
compared against the limit. A declared length that cannot be reduced to
one agreed value fails closed with HTTP 400 and
`{"error":"Request Content-Length is ambiguous"}`.
The ceiling applies to every method: an HTTP/2 GET, HEAD, or OPTIONS
request carrying DATA without Content-Length is forwarded through the
size-limited adapter, not replaced by an empty backend body (residual:
an HTTPS backend with HTTP/2 enabled whose target is not yet
capability-classified can negotiate HTTP/1.1 via ALPN and send an
unknown-length GET/HEAD bodyless until classified; pool warmup,
FERRUM_POOL_WARMUP_ENABLED, classifies targets up front).
Every 413 for this policy, from any plugin hook or from the proxy core's
streaming overrun, carries the one shared body
`{"error":"Request body exceeds maximum size"}` without the limit. A
Content-Length or buffered-body refusal by the plugin records
`request_size_limiting.reason`, `request_size_limiting.instance` (the
plugin-config id), `request_size_limiting.limit_bytes`, and (except for
an ambiguous Content-Length) `request_size_limiting.observed_bytes` in
request metadata. A final-body refusal records them only when its hook
receives a request context, on any protocol: always on the native
HTTP/3 preparation and HTTP/3 bridge paths, and elsewhere only when
another plugin on the route requests the final-body context. A
streaming overrun refused by the proxy core records none of them.

max_bytes.description: Maximum allowed request body size in bytes. Required and must be a positive JSON integer — the gateway rejects plugin creation when it is missing or null, 0, negative, fractional or in exponent form (for example 1048576.0), or not a number (for example "1048576"), with a diagnostic naming that fault class.
